text:
raj: Heads up — p95 decode latency +20% on canary after today's runtime merge (PR #4821). Dashboards spiked ~14:05 UTC.

emily: Seeing it on canary-4 as well. Repro locally with shortseq workload (seq <= 32).

kai: I ran a quick bisect, landing suspiciously on commit 4a7c2ef — the fused-op scheduler change. Reverting locally drops p95 back to baseline.

ci-bot: [perf-alert] decode_p95 increased 22% in canary pipeline (build 4821). Link: https://ci.internal/reports/4821

matthew: Can someone paste a small perf summary/flame so we have an idea (memcpy vs kernel time vs scheduler)? Also did KV eviction rates change?

raj: Quick profile from canary run (shortseq load):
```
Top hotspots:
 - memcpy: 48%
 - attention_kernel: 28%
 - scheduler/dispatch: 12%
 - kv-lookup: 6%
 - other: 6%
```

emily: memcpy being that high smells like an extra memcopy path got introduced in the fused op for short sequences. The PR altered the fuse->prefetch path to materialize a smaller tensor when <32 tokens, which triggers a host->device memcpy in the hot loop.

kai: Yep — I suspect we introduced synchronous copies when trying to avoid GPU scatter overhead. Could be pinned vs pageable memory choice too, causing stall on CUDA memcpy. Recommend `nsys` sample and `cudaMemcpy` stack traces.

anna: I'll open a revert PR now and start rolling canary back. Revert PR: #4833 (WIP).

raj: Before full revert, canary-test: set env `FUSE_MEMCOPY=0` to disable the new path and see if that mitigates. If so, we can hotfix selector quickly.

emily: Confirmed — FUSE_MEMCOPY=0 on canary-4 brings p95 within 3% of baseline. Temporary mitigation works.

kai: Good. I'll run `nsys` on the mitigated and unmitigated cases to capture whether memcpy is blocking kernel launches (NVTX traces). Sharing results shortly.

matthew: Hold rollout of today's merge to prod. No further canaries until we have either revert or a kernel-selector guard. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: Revert PR #4833 opened by anna. CI: pending (unit + perf smoke).

anna: Deploying revert to canary now, will post monitor links.

raj: Follow-up action items: add nightly perf test that runs shortseq workload and asserts device memcpy% < 20% for decode; add kernel-selector guard to avoid materializing small tensors on host for short sequences. Filed issue #523 for this.

emily: Added a short PR (draft) with the selector guard and a small unit test that toggles FUSE_MEMCOPY. Will link once ready.

kai: After we confirm `nsys` traces, I can propose a micro-optim to switch the copy path to async pinned memory and overlap with KV lookups.

matthew: Thanks all. Keep notifications here for rollback status.

ci-bot: Monitoring: canary revert deployment started at 14:26 UTC. Metrics: decode_p95 trending down (currently +2% vs baseline).

raj: Nice work. Once revert merges, let's run a perf bisect suite to ensure no regressions remain before resume.

emily: Filed issue and added test notes in the PR. Will follow-up with benchmark graphs.

anna: Revert merged to canary at 14:33 UTC. Monitoring looks good.

matthew: Planning a slow rollout after two green canary cycles. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
